annotations.annotation_text: Page 580 opens Book 3, Chapter 4 ("The Bedroom Scene") during the Age of Men (closing) phase. This passage continues HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream, featuring HCE, ALP, Shem, Shaun, Issy. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "customers" on page 580 ("The Bedroom Scene"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 580 ("The Bedroom Scene"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men (closing) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
